title: From Hourly to Annual: Tax, Super, and Salary Sacrifice Mortgage Explained
description: Convert your hourly rate to annual pay using the 38-hour week. Understand tax brackets, Medicare levy, super guarantee, and how a salary sacrifice mortgage can reduce taxable incom

faqs.q: How do I calculate my annual pay from my hourly rate?
faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work per week, then by 52. For a full-time employee on 38 hours, annual gross = hourly × 38 × 52. For example, at the National Minimum Wage of $26.44, annual pay is about $52,254.80. Use our [the timesheet](/) for a quick estimate.

faqs.q: What is the Medicare levy and how does it affect my take-home pay?
faqs.a: The Medicare levy is a 2% tax on your taxable income, used to fund Australia's public health system. It is added to your income tax. For a single person earning $52,254.80, the levy is $1,045.10. Some low-income earners may be eligible for a reduction. See our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) page for details.

faqs.q: Can I use salary sacrifice to reduce my taxable income for a mortgage?
faqs.a: Yes, a salary sacrifice mortgage arrangement allows you to direct pre-tax income into your home loan, lowering your taxable income. This can reduce the tax you pay and help you pay off your mortgage faster. However, it is not included in our calculator and requires employer agreement. Consult a tax professional for advice.

bodyMarkdown:
## Converting Your Hourly Rate to Annual Pay

If you earn an hourly wage or receive a salary offer, understanding your annual gross pay is essential for budgeting, tax planning, and considering strategies like a salary sacrifice mortgage. The basic formula is straightforward: multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work per week, then by 52 weeks. For a full-time employee, we assume a standard 38-hour week as set by the Fair Work Ombudsman. For example, the National Minimum Wage from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour, giving a weekly pay of $1,004.90 (38 hours × $26.44) and an annual gross of approximately $52,254.80 ($1,004.90 × 52). If you are a casual worker, your rate typically includes a 25% casual loading, making the minimum casual rate $33.05 per hour. Remember, the loading is added on top of the base rate – never type a rate that already includes casual loading into our [the timesheet](/) calculator.

### Fortnightly and Monthly Figures

Knowing your fortnightly pay can help with budgeting. Simply multiply your weekly pay by two. Using the minimum wage example, your fortnightly gross would be $2,009.80. This figure is useful when comparing salary offers or planning a salary sacrifice mortgage arrangement, where you redirect part of your pre-tax income towards your home loan. For higher earners, the Australian Bureau of Statistics reported that full-time adult ordinary time earnings averaged $2,083.70 per week in May 2026, giving a fortnightly gross of $4,167.40 and an annual gross of about $108,352.40. This is an average across all industries, not a median for any specific job – see our [average pay](/topics/average-pay) page for more context.

## Tax and the Medicare Levy

Once you have your annual gross, the next step is estimating your tax and Medicare levy. For the 2026–27 income year, the Australian Taxation Office applies a progressive tax scale:

- Nil tax on the first $18,200
- 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% on income from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% on income from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% on income above $190,000

In addition, most residents pay a Medicare levy of 2% of taxable income. The 2026–27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed at the time of this estimate, so we use the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds. For a single person earning $52,254.80, the tax would be approximately $5,092 (using the 15% and 30% brackets) plus Medicare levy of $1,045.10, giving a total of $6,137.10. Your take-home pay after tax and Medicare would be around $46,117.70. For a more precise calculation, see our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) guide.

### How Salary Sacrifice Mortgage Affects Tax

A salary sacrifice mortgage arrangement allows you to direct pre-tax income directly into your home loan, reducing your taxable income. For example, if you sacrifice $10,000 per year, your taxable income drops from $52,254.80 to $42,254.80, potentially lowering your tax bracket. This strategy can increase your disposable income and help you pay off your mortgage faster. However, salary sacrifice is not deducted in our calculator – it is a separate arrangement you negotiate with your employer. Always consult a tax professional.

## Super Guarantee Paid on Top

Your employer must pay super guarantee contributions of 12% of your ordinary earnings, on top of your salary. This is not deducted from your pay. For the minimum wage example, your employer would contribute an additional $6,270.58 per year (12% of $52,254.80), up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830. Super is a valuable part of your total remuneration package. Learn more about [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging).

### Award Rates and Casual Loading

The National Minimum Wage is the legal floor, but many employees are covered by awards or enterprise agreements that set higher rates. Award rates vary by industry and occupation and are determined by the Fair Work Commission. Casual employees receive a 25% loading in lieu of paid leave. Our [casual loading](/topics/casual-loading) page explains how to apply it correctly. If you are comparing a salary offer, ensure you know whether it includes super and whether you are entitled to penalty rates or allowances.

## Using the Hourly to Annual Calculator

Our [the timesheet](/) tool lets you enter your base hourly rate and optionally add casual loading. It calculates your weekly, fortnightly, and annual gross pay, then estimates tax, Medicare, and super. Remember, the result is an estimate. It assumes you work the same hours every week with no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. For a full breakdown of assumptions, see our [reference tables](/data).

### Key Points to Remember

- Annual pay = hourly rate × hours per week × 52. We assume 38 hours for full-time.
- Super is 12% paid on top, not deducted from your pay.
- Tax and Medicare are based on the 2026–27 resident rates.
- A salary sacrifice mortgage can reduce your taxable income, but is not included in our calculator.
- Always check your specific award or agreement with the Fair Work Ombudsman.
